in_arabic.name: شجاع
in_arabic.meaning: الشجاع اسم يعني الشخص الشجاع وال brave والقوي
in_arabic.long_meaning: الشجاع هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و معناه الشخص الشجاع وال brave والقوي، وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم في عدة مواضع، منها قول الله تعالى: 'وَكُلُّهُم أَتَوْهُ يَوْمَ القِيَامَةِ فَرْدًا' (سورة مريم: ٤٠)، وقد اشتق من جذر 'ش-ج-ع' الذي يعني الشجاعة وال courage. و الشجاع هو من الأسماء التي تطلق على الشخص الذي يمتلك الشجاعة وال courage في مواجهة التحديات والصعوبات.

in_english.name: Shujaah
in_english.long_meaning: Shujaah is a masculine given name originating from Arabic roots. It is derived from the 'sh-j-ʿ' root, conveying meanings of bravery, courage, and strength. In Islamic tradition, Shujaah symbolizes the qualities that enable a Muslim to face challenges with valor and resilience. The name has historical significance and is used across various Muslim cultures to denote someone with a strong and courageous personality.

data.cultural_impact: The name Shujaah signifies courage, bravery, and secular heroism. It is an honorable title for individuals who put themselves in harm's way to defend their communities, beliefs, and ideologies. It is a name that evokes images of warriors, leaders, and revolutionaries throughout Islamic history, such as Salahuddin Ayyubi, who brought the Islamic flag to Jerusalem, and Saif-Ud-Daula, who established the Sultanate of Bengal and defended it against foreign invasions. The name Shujaah continues to be a source of inspiration and pride for the Muslim community.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Shujaah goes beyond mere military valor or heroism. It speaks to the fundamental concept of justice and standing up for what is right, not only for oneself but also for others. The Quran encourages Muslims to be "Shujaa," striving in the cause of Allah (76:21). The prophet Muhammad (PBUH) himself was a Shujaah, bravely preaching and defending the Islamic faith, even in the face of persecution. By striving in the path of Allah and promoting justice, a person named Shujaah not only earns worldly respect but also gains the pleasure and blessings of Allah. The name serves as a reminder to constantly strive for the betterment of oneself and the community, and to be a beacon of courage and resilience in the face of adversity.
